correctness.rationale: For every fixed integer d>=2 and real 1<p<2, Euclidean diameter 2 is achieved only by d coordinate-axis pairs. The endpoint deficit is uniformly (sum |u|^p+sum |v|^p)/p times (1+o(1)); the line-coordinate Jacobian is 2^{-(d-1)} at each axis, and Crofton/Cauchy gives total hitting measure kappa_{d-1}S_p/2. Scaling by (p epsilon)^{1/p} integrates the unit l_p ball of dimension 2(d-1), yielding the stated coefficient and conditional uniform law; the Dirichlet transformation follows by its explicit density. Exact numerical chord evaluations and Jacobian checks corroborate but do not substitute for proof.

value.rationale: The family is a classical continuous and natural geometric interpolation from polytope-like axial singularity toward the Euclidean sphere, but the sharp exponent 2(d-1)/p and explicit normalized coefficient are not inherited from either the positive-curvature or polyhedral formulas. The conditional Dirichlet endpoint law resolves geometric information missing from unmarked chord-length probabilities and suggests a quantitative local universality principle. This is a structural exact theorem across every dimension and real p in (1,2), not an arbitrary finite computation.
